key_insight: Lattice Boltzmann can be viewed as a rule-driven information-processing machine whose physics-constrained iterations generate closed macroscopic transport laws.
engineering_relevance: This perspective offers a framework for adding physics-based or learned components to LB models while preserving the properties needed for macroscopic closure.
method: Interpret local relaxation followed by lattice streaming as iterated relaxation dynamics related to residual networks and transformers.
Identify three update properties sufficient for macroscopic closure, with the local target determining the resulting law.
Test the framework using random targets on a lattice and a traffic-trained network on a graph.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that random targets generate transport laws predicted by their moments and that a graph network trained on traffic generates a conservation law, but provides no quantitative metrics.
watch_item: Damping of non-conserved modes can fail without warning from the lattice-level macroscopic law, so macroscopic agreement alone is not a sufficient stability check.
